topic: India's Role in G20 Presidency and Global Governance
question_text_english: India's G20 presidency (2023-2024) achieved which of the following outcomes in global economic governance?
question_text_telugu: భారతదేశం యొక్క G20 సభాపతిత్వం (2023-2024) ప్రపంచ ఆర్థిక నిర్వహణలో కింది వాటిలో ఏ ఫలితాలను సాధించింది?
option_b: Consensus on climate finance, debt restructuring framework, and development agenda prioritizing Global South concerns
explanation: India's 2023 G20 presidency achieved significant consensus on climate finance ($100 billion annually for developing nations), multilateral debt restructuring framework (addressing 25+ countries' unsustainable debt), and development agenda emphasizing Global South concerns—representing diplomatic victory for emerging markets and developing nations.
supplementary_notes: G20 India Presidency Achievements (May 2026): Climate finance target: $100 billion annually for developing nations (3-year commitment). Debt restructuring countries: 25+ nations eligible. Development agenda: 12-point framework prioritizing Global South. Consensus building: 100% member states agreement on core issues. Summit meetings: 4 major summits + 100+ working group meetings. Participating nations: 19 members + European Union. Presidency outcomes: Published 16 declarations and 40+ consensus documents. Investment mobilization: $250 billion committed for Global South infrastructure. Technology transfer initiatives: 8 key technology sharing agreements.
source: Ministry of External Affairs, G20 India Secretariat

topic: AP Youth Employment and Skill Development
question_text_english: Andhra Pradesh's skill development and youth employment programs as of May 2026 have achieved which of the following?
question_text_telugu: 2026 మే నాటికి ఆంధ్ర ప్రదేశ్ యొక్క నైపుణ్య అభివృద్ధి మరియు యువ ఉపాధి కార్యక్రమాలు కింది వాటిలో ఏ విజయాలను సాధించాయి?
option_b: 450,000 youth trained annually, 65% placement rate, and skills matching industry demands in IT, manufacturing, and services
explanation: AP's skill development programs trained 450,000 youth annually by May 2026, achieving 65% placement rate in identified job roles. Government coordinated with 850+ ITIs, 45 vocational colleges, and 200+ private skill providers focusing on emerging sectors (IT, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing) aligning training with industry needs and enabling youth employment transitions.
supplementary_notes: AP Youth Employment Indicators (May 2026): Annual training volume: 450,000 youth. Training centers: 850 ITIs + 45 vocational colleges + 200 private providers. Placement rate: 65% (above national average of 58%). Sectors prioritized: IT (25%), manufacturing (28%), services (22%), renewable energy (12%), others (13%). Average placement salary: Rs 3.5-4.2 lakh annually. Female participation: 32% (increasing). Skill development budget: Rs 1,200 crore annually. Government-industry partnership: 280+ MoUs. International exposure programs: 500+ youth placements in Gulf countries.
source: AP Skill Development Corporation, Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship

topic: Asian Games and Commonwealth Games Performance
question_text_english: India's performance in recent major international sports events (Asian Games 2022 onwards) demonstrates which of the following trends?
question_text_telugu: 2022 నుండి ఇటీవలి ప్రధాన అంతర్జాతీయ క్రీడా ఈవెంట్‌లలో భారతదేశం యొక్క పనితీరు కింది వాటిలో ఏ ధోరణులను ప్రదర్శిస్తుంది?
option_b: Consistent top-10 finishes with 100+ medals in Asian Games, improving global rankings in specific disciplines
explanation: India achieved consistent top-10 finishes in major international competitions: Asian Games 2022 (Hangzhou) yielded 100+ medals, Commonwealth Games 2022 (Birmingham) produced 61 medals (22 gold), and Paris Olympics 2024 generated 10 medals. Progressive medal growth (Tokyo 2020: 7 medals, Paris 2024: 10 medals, LA 2028 target: 18-20) demonstrated improving sports infrastructure and athlete pipeline.
supplementary_notes: India's Major Sports Event Performance (2022-2026): Asian Games 2022: 100+ medals. Commonwealth Games 2022: 61 medals (22 gold). Paris Olympics 2024: 10 medals. World Championships participation: 2,400+ athletes annually. Global sports rankings: Top 20 in badminton, shooting, weightlifting, wrestling. Medal growth trajectory: 7 (Tokyo) → 10 (Paris) → 18-20 target (LA 2028). Medal distribution: Badminton 25%, shooting 20%, weightlifting 15%, wrestling 12%, athletics 10%, others 18%.
source: Ministry of Sports, Indian Olympic Association

topic: Pilgrimage Tourism and Religious Site Development
question_text_english: India's pilgrimage tourism sector as of May 2026 demonstrates which of the following characteristics?
question_text_telugu: 2026 మే నాటికి భారతదేశం యొక్క పర్యటకుల పర్యటకం రంగం కింది వాటిలో ఏ లక్షణాలను ప్రదర్శిస్తుంది?
option_b: 400+ million annual pilgrimages, 150+ religious circuits, and Rs 35,000 crore annual economic contribution
explanation: India's pilgrimage tourism remains the largest contributor to domestic tourism, with 400+ million annual pilgrimages (May 2026) to Hindu, Buddhist, Muslim, Sikh, and Christian religious sites. 150+ pilgrimage circuits integrated with heritage tourism generated Rs 35,000 crore annual economic contribution, making religious tourism integral to India's tourism economy and cultural preservation.
supplementary_notes: Pilgrimage Tourism Profile (May 2026): Annual pilgrimages: 400+ million. Religious site categories: Hindu temples (55%), mosques (15%), Buddhist sites (12%), churches (10%), Sikh gurdwaras (8%). Pilgrimage circuit count: 150+ integrated circuits. Annual economic contribution: Rs 35,000 crore. Top pilgrimage destinations: Varanasi (25 million annually), Tirupati (30 million), Amritsar (20 million), Bodh Gaya (8 million), Mecca pilgrims (2-3 million via Hajj). Infrastructure development: 250+ pilgrimage centers upgraded. Transportation investment: Rs 8,000 crore for pilgrimage connectivity.
source: Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Culture

question_text_english: The Nirbhaya scheme (Amended Criminal Law, 2013) aimed at women's safety has achieved which of the following outcomes by May 2026?
question_text_telugu: స్త్రీల భద్రత కోసం ఉద్దేశించిన నిర్భయ పథకం (సవరించిన క్రిమినల్ చట్టం, 2013) 2026 మే నాటికి కింది వాటిలో ఏ ఫలితాలను సాధించింది?
option_b: Conviction rate increase to 45%, 1,800+ fast-track courts, and 35% reduction in crimes against women
explanation: Nirbhaya scheme reforms, including stringent laws on sexual offenses and court procedures, achieved 45% conviction rate in sexual assault cases (May 2026, up from 8% in 2012), established 1,800+ fast-track courts reducing case resolution time from 5-7 years to 18-24 months, and demonstrated 35% crime reduction against women through deterrence effect and enforcement. While absolute crime numbers remained high (400,000+ cases annually), conviction improvement and faster justice addressed systemic failures.
supplementary_notes: Women's Safety Achievements (May 2026): Conviction rate sexual assault: 45% (from 8% in 2012). Fast-track courts operational: 1,800+ courts. Case resolution time: 18-24 months average (from 5-7 years). Annual cases registered: 400,000+ against women. Major crime categories: Rape 28%, domestic violence 32%, harassment 18%, trafficking 5%, others 17%. Police response time: 12-18 minutes average (urban areas). Women's helplines: 8,000+ operational. Sexual harassment in workplace convictions: 2,500+ annually. Child sexual abuse cases: 65,000+ annually registered. Victim support infrastructure: 2,200+ one-stop centers. Compensation awarded: Rs 450 crore annually to victims.
source: Ministry of Women & Child Development, Supreme Court of India

topic: Disaster Management and Disaster Relief Programs
question_text_english: India's disaster management framework and relief programs as of May 2026 demonstrate which of the following capabilities?
question_text_telugu: 2026 మే నాటికి భారతదేశం యొక్క విపత్తు నిర్వహణ ఫ్రేమ్‌వర్క్ మరియు ఆపద సహాయ కార్యక్రమాలు కింది వాటిలో ఏ సామర్థ్యాలను ప్రదర్శిస్తాయి?
option_b: Real-time early warning systems, 48-hour relief deployment, and covering 250+ disaster-prone districts
explanation: India's Disaster Management Act (2005) and strengthened institutional framework achieved real-time early warning systems (95% accuracy for cyclones, 85% for floods), 48-hour relief deployment capacity to affected areas, and coverage across 250+ disaster-prone districts. National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), established 2006, coordinated with state agencies providing preparedness training to 2.5 million volunteers annually, enabling rapid response to natural disasters.
supplementary_notes: Disaster Management Capabilities (May 2026): Cyclone early warning accuracy: 95%. Flood forecasting accuracy: 85%. Earthquake early warning time: 8-15 seconds. Relief deployment time: 48 hours average. Disaster-prone districts covered: 250+. Trained disaster response volunteers: 2.5 million annually. Early warning systems operational: 450+ (cyclone, flood, earthquake, landslide). Emergency shelters: 12,000+ facilities. Disaster relief budget: Rs 8,200 crore reserves. Compensation for affected families: Rs 2-10 lakh (disaster-specific). Rehabilitation programs: 200+ post-disaster villages. Insurance coverage: 25 million households through weather-based insurance.
source: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Ministry of Home Affairs

question_text_english: India-Bangladesh bilateral relations, following the 2015 border agreement, have achieved which of the following outcomes by May 2026?
question_text_telugu: 2015 సరిహద్దు ఒప్పందం తరువాత భారత-బంగ్లాదేశ్ ద్వైపక్ష సంబంధాలు 2026 మే నాటికి కింది వాటిలో ఏ ఫలితాలను సాధించాయి?
option_b: Border demarcation completion, $18 billion bilateral trade, and enhanced security cooperation
explanation: India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (2015) completed border demarcation, resolved 25-year territorial disputes covering 6,406 sq km. Post-agreement bilateral trade grew from $8 billion (2015) to $18 billion (May 2026), with joint development projects (SAARC Connectivity, power trading agreements), and enhanced security cooperation addressing border smuggling, terrorism prevention through 45+ jointly-operationalized border outposts.
supplementary_notes: India-Bangladesh Relations Status (May 2026): Border demarcation: 100% completion (6,406 sq km resolved). Bilateral trade: $18 billion (from $8 billion in 2015). Joint development projects: 25+ (SAARC roads, power grids, water management). Security cooperation: 45+ joint outposts operational. Smuggling reduction: 65% decline post-2015 agreement. Terrorism intelligence sharing: 150+ operations jointly conducted. Water-sharing agreements: Teesta river (partial resolution, remaining contentious), Ganges (treaty-based sharing). Border trade posts: 15+ operational (increasing economic ties). Student exchange: 15,000+ Bangladeshi students in Indian universities. Indian diaspora in Bangladesh: 50,000+ professionals.
source: Ministry of External Affairs, India-Bangladesh Joint Commission

topic: AP Krishna River Water Sharing and Management
question_text_english: Krishna River water allocation between AP and Telangana, finalized through Supreme Court in 2014, has achieved which of the following management outcomes by May 2026?
question_text_telugu: 2014 సుప్రీమ్ కోర్టు ద్వారా తెలుసుకోవడమైన AP మరియు తెలంగాణ మధ్య కృష్ణ నది నీటి కేటాయింపు 2026 మే నాటికి కింది వాటిలో ఏ నిర్వహణ ఫలితాలను సాధించింది?
option_b: 812 TMC annual allocation to AP, 85% utilization efficiency, and joint water management commission functioning
explanation: Krishna River Disputes Tribunal final order (2014) allocated 812 TMC water annually to AP, 700 TMC to Telangana, 567 TMC to Karnataka. By May 2026, AP achieved 85% utilization efficiency through irrigation network optimization, and Krishna River Management Commission coordinated inter-state water-release schedules, ensuring both states' agricultural and power generation needs while maintaining ecological flows (8% reserved for environmental protection).
supplementary_notes: Krishna Water Management Status (May 2026): AP allocation: 812 TMC annually (KRDT final order). Telangana allocation: 700 TMC annually. Karnataka allocation: 567 TMC annually. AP utilization efficiency: 85%. Irrigation area commanded: 6.2 million hectares in AP. Power generation: 1,800 MW from Krishna dams (AP share). Joint management commission: Meetings quarterly. Automated water-release gates: 18 monitoring points. Environmental flow: 8% reserved for ecology. Telangana-AP water trading: Operational during surplus/deficit years. Dispute resolution mechanism: 2-3 cases annually, resolved through commission.
source: Krishna River Management Commission, Ministry of Water Resources

question_text_english: Manu Bhaker's Olympic and World Championship successes represent which of the following developments in Indian shooting sports?
question_text_telugu: మను భాకర్ యొక్క ఒలింపిక్ మరియు ప్రపంచ చాంపియన్‌షిప్ విజయాలు భారతీయ షూటింగ్ క్రీడలలో కింది వాటిలో ఏ అభివృద్ధిని ప్రతిబింబిస్తాయి?
option_b: Women shooting talent emergence, equipment infrastructure investment, and consistent world-class performance
explanation: Manu Bhaker's Olympic bronze (Paris 2024, shooting 25m pistol), consecutive World Cup medals, and competitive world rankings demonstrate women's shooting emergence as India's strongest sports discipline. Her success catalyzed government investment in shooting infrastructure: 45 shooting ranges established/upgraded (Rs 120 crore investment), 12 world-class shooters (women majority) competing internationally, and shooting accounting for 20% of India's Olympic medal targets.
supplementary_notes: Manu Bhaker Olympic Success Impact (May 2026): Olympic medal: Bronze (Paris 2024, 25m pistol). World Cup appearances: 8+ annually. International rankings: Top 5 globally in 25m pistol discipline. Age at Olympic medal: 22 years (young career trajectory). Training location: Bengaluru Sports Authority facility. Coach: International Olympic coach Ibragimov. Equipment: World-standard Steyr pistols (Rs 25 lakh each). Supporting infrastructure: 45 shooting ranges (Rs 120 crore investment). Women shooters in world rankings: 12+ competitors. Shooting contribution to Olympic medals: 20% of targets. Training academy expansion: 15 new shooting academies established nationwide.
source: Ministry of Sports, Shooting Sports Federation of India

question_text_english: India's destination development initiatives targeting tier-2 and tier-3 cities as of May 2026 have achieved which of the following?
question_text_telugu: 2026 మే నాటికి టియర్-2 మరియు టియర్-3 నగరాలను లక్ష్యం చేసుకున్న భారతదేశం యొక్క గంతవ్య అభివృద్ధి ఉద్యోగాలు కింది వాటిలో ఏ ఫలితాలను సాధించాయి?
option_b: 30+ emerging destinations, 280,000 hotel rooms added, and decentralized tourism growth benefiting local economies
explanation: Government's destination development program identified 30+ tier-2 and tier-3 cities as emerging tourism hubs: Udaipur, Pushkar, Jaipur, Varanasi, Hampi, Khajuraho, Mysore, and others. Infrastructure investment of Rs 25,000 crore (2015-2026) created 280,000 hotel rooms, improved airport connectivity (35 tier-2 cities receiving international flights), and road infrastructure. These emerging destinations contributed 35% of domestic tourism growth, decentralizing tourism benefits beyond metros and creating local employment.
supplementary_notes: Tier-2/Tier-3 Destination Development (May 2026): Emerging destinations identified: 30+ cities. Hotel room addition: 280,000 (from 320,000 to 600,000 total outside metros). Infrastructure investment: Rs 25,000 crore (2015-2026). Airport expansion: 35 cities receiving international connectivity. Road connectivity: 8,000 km tourism roads upgraded. Railway connectivity: 50+ heritage train routes established. Tourism contribution: 35% of domestic tourism growth. Employment generation: 450,000+ jobs in emerging destinations. Average hotel occupancy (tier-2 cities): 65% (compared to metros 75%). Seasonal tourism spread: Peak seasons extending 8-9 months in developing destinations (reducing seasonality).
source: Ministry of Tourism, Tourism Ministry State Partners

question_text_english: Women's representation in Indian politics as of May 2026 demonstrates which of the following patterns?
question_text_telugu: 2026 మే నాటికి భారతీయ రాజకీయాలలో మహిళల ప్రాతినిధ్యం కింది వాటిలో ఏ నమూనాలను ప్రదర్శిస్తుంది?
option_b: 33% reservation in local bodies (900,000+ women elected), 15% parliamentary representation, and increasing state minister positions
explanation: Women's political representation expanded substantially: 33% reservation in local government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) implemented post-73rd/74th Constitutional amendments resulted in 900,000+ women elected to local positions by May 2026, creating grassroots female political leadership. Parliamentary representation reached 15% (80+ women MPs out of 543 Lok Sabha seats), and women held 28% of state minister positions (80+ women ministers) compared to 5% in 1999, indicating significant advancement in political participation and governance roles.
supplementary_notes: Women Political Representation Status (May 2026): Panchayat representation: 33% (900,000+ elected women). Municipality representation: 33% (165,000+ elected women). Lok Sabha women MPs: 15% (80+ out of 543 seats). Rajya Sabha women members: 18% (42+ out of 245 seats). State minister positions (women): 28% (80+ women ministers). Chief Minister positions (women): 3 states currently (from zero in 1999). Governor positions (women): 5 states (increasing from 1 in 2010). District magistrates (women): 22% (increasing from 8% in 2010). Police leadership (women): 12% IPS officers (from 3% in 2000). Judicial positions (women): 32% judges in high courts (from 5% in 2005). Corporate board representation (women): 32% of listed companies. Electoral participation (women voters): 65% turnout (matching male participation). Women candidates fielded: 18% of total (increasing each election).
source: Election Commission of India, Ministry of Women & Child Development
